newsitem.title: CANADA: Investors to buy TimberWest for C$674 mln.
newsitem.headline: Investors to buy TimberWest for C$674 mln.

text.p: TimberWest Forest Ltd said Friday that it abandoned its efforts to transform itself into a royalty trust and instead agreed to sell out to an investor group for C$22 a share or C$674 million.
The lumber company said that as part of the deal it would also sell some of its operations to rival Slocan Forest Products Ltd for C$200 million plus assumed debt.
TimberWest chief executive Keith Purchase said the buyout offer from TAL Acquisition Ltd was unsolicited.

"Although TimberWest was in the process of creating its own timberland income fund...the directors were obligated, on behalf of all shareholders, to evaluate this new offer," he said. "After consideration of all factors, the board determined today that the TAL cash offer for 100 percent of TimberWest's shares provides greater value to shareholders."
The investor syndicate is sponsored by Goepel Shields & Partners Inc. in cooperation with TD Securities Inc., TD Capital Group Ltd., and the Toronto Dominion Bank.
TimberWest said TAL is "indirectly owned by a cross section of Canadian institutional investors which have committed C$300 million in equity to the deal."
Officials were not available for further comment but one industry source said the institutions planned to create their own royalty trust from the remnants of TimberWest.

TimberWest is 52 percent owned by Fletcher Challenge Canada Ltd, which in turn is controlled by New Zealand's Fletcher Challenge Ltd. Fletcher Canada in October precipiated an effort to find a buyer for TimberWest.
That was dropped in January in favor of a plan to sell TimberWest's private timberlands into the capital market by way of an income fund and distribute proceeds to shareholders.
Fletcher, which wants to focus more on its paper business, said Friday it supported the latest buyout offer because its all-cash nature was more advantageous.
Its stake in TimberWest is worth C$348 million under the deal. Timberwest will also refinance its existing C$210 million in debt to Fletcher Canada.
The deal must be approved by 75 percent of TimberWest shareholders and approval by the British Columbia government.
TimberWest shareholders are expected to meet in early May and, if approved, the takeover would close in late May.

Slocan is buying TimberWest's sawmilling and timber operations at Mackenzie and Williams Lake in the interior of British Columbia, as well as its railway tie treatment plant at Ashcroft, British Columbia.
Slocan said the deal would strengthen its stature as a lumber producer in the interior region. It expects to fund the acquisition by equal amounts of debt and equity financing.
The sawmills have combined capacity of 500 million board feet of lumber and associated annual timber harvesting rights of 2.1 million cubic metres.
The wood chip production from both operations is contracted to Fletcher Challenge's pulp mill in Mackenzie.
The deal was announced after the market closed Friday. Earlier TimberWest stock closed up 0.40 at 20.95 in Toronto. Slocan shares eased 0.15 to 14.40.
